...
} ``` ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher export const prefetch = 'partial' export default function Page() { return
...
} ``` ## Options ### `'partial'` Opts the segment into [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) without enabling the global [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) flag. A `` pointing at a segment with `prefetch = 'partial'` loads the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) instead of the legacy full prefetch. Set this on the destination, not the link. For links that opt into a wider prefetch with [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), Next.js uses per-link prefetching. The server renders a fresh response that resolves URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL). On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves prefetches from the static cache. If a page accesses non-static data, it's prefetched at runtime. Use this for incremental adoption when you can't enable `partialPrefetching` for the entire app at once. Once every route in scope has `prefetch = 'partial'`, enable the global flag and remove the per-route exports. > **Good to know**: When Next.js performs a per-link prefetch for a segment, all downstream segments are included in the same request. {"session_id":null,"state":"completed","backend":"captured","persistence":"process","output_truncated":true,"output_incomplete":false,"output_terminal_safe":true,"full_output_handle":"fx-command-replay-794203b15e9caf52aea867c8d4556996-74e5dfdd6a04dd5a.bin","exit_code":0,"signal":null,"termination_indeterminate":false,"duration_ms":14,"accepted_bytes":null,"error":null,"retry_guidance":null,"output_delta":"--- title: prefetch description: API Reference for the prefetch function, which keeps a subtree out of a route's App Shell so it renders on a per-link prefetch or a navigation. related: links: - app/api-reference/functions/navigation - app/api-reference/functions/connection - app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching - app/api-reference/functions/io - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents --- Calling `await prefetch()` defers the code below it to a per-link prefetch or a navigation, instead of rendering it in the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The fallback of the nearest [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary takes its place in the shell, and the deferred content renders once one of those happens. It is meant to defer content that the App Shell would otherwise render, typically content that depends on session data and is expensive to generate. During a build-time prerender nothing is deferred, so content below `prefetch()` is prerendered as usual. ## Usage The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5} import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } export default nextConfig ``` A route is then rendered in three stages, and content can arrive at any of them: 1. The App Shell, which every `` into the route prefetches, and which holds the part of the route that does not depend on the URL. 2. A per-link prefetch, requested with [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), which resolves the URL and adds the content that depends on it. 3. The navigation itself, which covers everything left. Awaiting `prefetch()` keeps content out of the App Shell, so it renders only on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation. To keep content out of per-link prefetches as well, so it renders only on the navigation, use [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation). Everything above `prefetch()` renders in the App Shell, and everything below renders on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation. Deferral is scoped to the component that awaits it and the tree below: sibling branches render in the shell as usual. Place it above the work to defer, and wrap the component in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense): ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" highlight={25} switcher import { Suspense } from 'react' import { cookies } from 'next/headers' import { cacheLife, prefetch } from 'next/cache' export default function Page() { return ( <> Loading greeting...

}> {/* in the App Shell */} Loading recommendations...

}> {/* the fallback is in the App Shell, the recommendations are not */} ) } async function Greeting() { const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value return

{session ? 'Welcome back' : 'Welcome'}

} async function Recommendations()

events.content:
The dashboard links now prefetch only the project's title. The description and activity list load when you click through. `npx next build` passes (exit 0), but I haven't checked what actually gets prefetched in a browser. Prefetching only runs in production (`next build && next start`), not `next dev`.

**Changes:**

1. **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`**
   - Added `export const prefetch = 'partial'`. This turns on partial prefetching for this page only, so the rest of the app is unaffected.
   - Moved the title into its own `<ProjectTitle>` component with its own loading boundary. It reads the slug and calls `getProjectTitle`, which is cached, so it can be fetched before the click.
   - Moved the description and activity into `<ProjectDetails>`, which starts with `await navigation()`. Nothing after that line runs during a prefetch, so the slow `getProjectDetails` call (800 ms) only runs when you actually navigate. Until then, its "Loading details..." placeholder shows.

2. **`app/page.tsx`**: the dashboard links now use `<Link prefetch={true}>`. This is what fetches the title ahead of the click. A default link would only fetch the parts of the page that don't depend on the URL, and the title depends on the slug.

I followed the bundled docs for `prefetch`, `navigation()` and partial prefetching in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`, and checked that the installed version (16.4.0-canary.52) includes `navigation`.

The build also rewrote `tsconfig.json`, which was unchanged before, so I restored it with `git checkout`. It also left build output behind: `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts`, neither of which is in `.gitignore`. Your existing changes (`package.json` and the untracked files) weren't touched.
